topic: Agent Memory Layer Comparison 2026: Déjà Vu vs Mem0 vs Zep vs Agent Memory MCP

Full-context retrieval: 9.87s median, 17.12s p95 latency vs 1.44s p95 for memory systems (12x improvement)
90% token savings vs full-context approaches

angles: Déjà Vu is the newest entrant (July 2026) — a zero-dependency Go binary that repurposes existing agent session logs as a searchable memory layer, requiring no separate service or database setup
The MCP ecosystem has exploded: Engram, Nocturne Memory, Stash, mcp-mem0, and Memory Bank MCP all provide memory via the Model Context Protocol, making them agent-agnostic
MemPalace (57k+ stars) is the surprise breakout of 2026 — local-first, MIT, beating cloud incumbents on benchmarks with zero API calls
The fundamental architectural divide: vector+graph+KV (Mem0) vs temporal knowledge graph (Zep) vs OS-tiered paging (Letta) vs local-first verbatim (MemPalace) vs retroactive log-based (Déjà Vu)
Lock-in risk is the hidden cost: Mem0 is low (SDK swap), Letta is high (runtime replacement), Déjà Vu is minimal (just a binary + MCP config)
Verbatim storage (MemPalace, Déjà Vu) vs summarization (Mem0, Zep) — a fundamental trade-off between recall accuracy and storage efficiency
